spoken: [hook] Your gym plan doesn't fail on day one. It fails around day four. || On day one you're excited, so you just go. By day four the excitement is gone, and the question, when do I go today, gets answered by your mood. And your mood usually says tomorrow. || [turn] So don't let it decide. Keep the plan, and give every session a fixed time, like a meeting you wouldn't skip. || Here's how. On Sunday evening, open your calendar and book three sessions. Monday at seven, push. Wednesday at seven, pull. Friday at seven, legs. Forty five minutes each. || Now day four isn't a decision anymore. Thursday is rest, you already know that. And Friday at seven, it's legs. Your mood doesn't get a vote. || And if you miss one, move it, don't delete it. Missed Wednesday? It goes to Thursday at seven. || [land] So do it this Sunday. Three sessions, three times, in your calendar before the week starts. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.

caption.instagram:
Your gym plan doesn't fail on day one. It fails around day four, when the excitement is gone and your mood decides when you go.

The fix:
• Sunday evening, book 3 sessions in your calendar
• Mon 7:00 push, Wed 7:00 pull, Fri 7:00 legs, 45 min each
• Missed one? Move it, don't delete it
